title: [Autour de La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois, pages 1 à 67] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page finishes the proof, begun on page 32, of an injectivity theorem. For a variety X over an absolutely finitely generated field K, the map from K-points to Galois-equivariant classes, X(K) → H^1(K, π1(X̄)), is injective. Equivalently, distinct points give non-conjugate sections of the fundamental group extension. Note that p. 32 is about H^1(K, H_1(X̄)) (the abelianization), and its claim that the second (abelian) map suffices also needs the Albanese reduction.

By p. 32 the problem is reduced to G = a semi-abelian variety (an extension of an abelian variety by a torus), with H_1(Ḡ) = T(G) = lim_n nG, the full Tate module. The map (16) is then the Kummer homomorphism G(K) → H^1(K, T(G)). Its composite with H^1(K, T(G)) → lim H^1(K, nG) factors as G(K) → lim G(K)/n ↪ lim H^1(K, nG), using the Kummer sequences 0 → nG → G → G → 0.

This page:
- The kernel is ∩_n n·G(K), the infinitely divisible elements.
- Since K is absolutely finitely generated, Mordell–Weil (in the Lang–Néron form) is invoked to say G(K) is a finitely generated Z-module. Hence G(K) → lim G(K)/n is injective, and so is (16). QED.

Remark: it would not suffice to look at the extension of E_{K/k} (the arithmetic fundamental group) by a single ℓ-adic H_1(X, Z_ℓ); all ℓ are needed. A point of order p ≠ ℓ (prime-to-ℓ torsion) is killed by the ℓ-adic Kummer map, so translation by it gives a counterexample.

The result is then reformulated torsor-theoretically. For x ∈ G(K), take the torsor under T_∞(G) = lim nG given by the fibre over x of the 'universal abelian covering' G̃ = lim (G → G under multiplication by n). The statement says: if this torsor is trivial (x lifts at every level n), then x = 0.

The next page discusses what happens in characteristic p: p-torsion, radicial (purely inseparable) liftings, working 'up to finite radicial surjective morphisms', and the prime-to-p fundamental group, where injectivity fails.
errors: As written, 'G(K) is of finite type' is false when G has a torus part. For example G_m(Q) = Q^* is not finitely generated.

The conclusion still holds, because the multiplicative group K^* of a finitely generated field is a free abelian group modulo its finite torsion, so it has no nontrivial divisible elements. The abelian part is handled by Lang–Néron. So what is needed is 'no nonzero infinitely divisible elements', not finite generation.
The claim on p. 32 that X can be reduced to a semi-abelian G implicitly uses a generalized Albanese and the reduction of the first map to the second. This is fine but not detailed here.

ideas.what: Injectivity of the map from K-points to sections (classes in H^1(K, π1)) for absolutely finitely generated K, via the Kummer map on the (generalized) Albanese and Mordell–Weil/Lang–Néron
ideas.modern_name: injectivity part of the section conjecture / 'elementary' injectivity of the section map
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (letter to Faltings, 1983); standard in the literature (e.g. Stix's book 'Rational points and arithmetic of fundamental groups')
ideas.where_published: Letter to Faltings (27 June 1983), in Geometric Galois Actions vol. 1

ideas.what: Kernel of the Kummer map G(K) → lim H^1(K, nG) equals the infinitely divisible elements ∩ nG(K)
A single ℓ-adic (pro-ℓ abelian) fundamental group does not detect points: translation by prime-to-ℓ torsion gives non-injectivity, so the full profinite group is needed
ideas.modern_name: failure of injectivity for pro-ℓ / ℓ-adic section maps
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore; discussed in section conjecture literature

ideas.what: Reformulation: x = 0 iff the T_∞(G)-torsor given by the fibre of the universal abelian cover over x is trivial
ideas.modern_name: fibre of the adelic Tate-module cover / Kummer torsor

deep.surprise_reason: This is a standard, now well-known argument, close to what Grothendieck wrote to Faltings in 1983. Its only flaw is a minor imprecision about tori. The remark that all ℓ are needed is folklore.
transcription_corrections: Top insertion: 'est ∩_n n H^0(K,G), donc' should precede 'le noyau est formé…', with 'G' standing for G(K).
Insertion above line 5 is likely 'Z-module de' rather than 'Z[?]', giving 'le th. de Mordell-Weil nous [dit/assure] que G(K) est un Z-module de type fini'.
Start of the Remark: 'Je ne réfléchis pas dans [?] est engendrée en regardant' is more plausibly 'Il ne suffirait pas dans [cet énoncé] de regarder, pour un ℓ, l'extension…'.
'sinon [?] p' is probably 'sinon si ℓ ≠ p', referring to a point of order p prime to ℓ.
'image δ_x [?], du groupe': the symbol at the line start is uncertain; it may be 'K'.
